heuristics.statement: The first blocks M0 are fresh uniform 512-bit strings (two uniform 256-bit words each); their chaining values CV1 = F_38(IV, M0) behave as independent uniform 256-bit values. Consequences used: for every fixed variant a0, Pr[W7x in F7] = p7 = 287,309,824/2^32 exactly, and given it (W0..W6) is uniform and independent of W7 (Lemma 5.1); E16x is uniform for a good pair, so a lane passes the 8 tested bits with probability 2^-8 and the row-16 set with probability 160/2^32; the expected numbers of passing classes (0.53516 for the 8 accepted classes, 3.2110 for the 48 of this revision) and good pairs (13,152; 64,116 for the 48) per first block; independence across first blocks.
heuristics.scope: The expected counts per first block that fix the work (V_MAX), the law of the second-block words that defines q3, and the independence of the first blocks (proof.md Sections 5 and 10).
heuristics.extrapolation: Exact distribution of the number of passing classes over all 2^32 values of A_{-1} for the 8 classes (p8hits.c, Appendix A.2); 29,360,128 (2^22 + 2^23 + 2^24) real first blocks through the attack's own filters with the 8 classes (proof.md Section 13.1, e2ep8.c): passing classes, good pairs and stage-3a passes within 0.07% of their expectations, 14,199 row-16 passes against 14,385.0 expected (z = -1.55), every one checked exactly in Python (the first block gives the chaining value, the variant is selected, rows -4..16 hold in both members); the organizer experiment a0-online-r38. The 48-class revision (Appendix D) applies the same per-variant law to 48 H-closed classes; Section D.7 measures q3 per class and finds no class dependence, and the ledger charges Pr[some class passes] as 1 on every block, so no exact class-pass distribution is used (Section D.8).
heuristics.limitations: A premise, not a theorem; tested on 2^24 first blocks, not 2^82. The class tests of one first block are correlated (at most 2 of the 32 maximal classes pass); only the expectations and the exact probability that some class passes enter the ledger.

heuristics.statement: For a good pair, q3 is the average over all 958,464 selected variants of the probability of the accepted event: rows 16..21 follow every P8 A/E/W cell, accepted '+' pair and two-bit condition, with row 19 on its signed differences and E18=E17 on bits 24, 23 and 15 not imposed; after step 37 A34..A37 and E34..E37 match. The direct mode-c lower-bound measurement gives q3 >= q3_model = 2^-95.7601.
heuristics.scope: The expected successes E[X] = N_FB g q3 and N_FB. The derivative proof's leading section supersedes the inherited composite q3 in Sections 7, 10 through 12 and Appendix D.8.
heuristics.extrapolation: A preregistration with SHA-256 3b35e14b... froze the audited C source hash 0bc7cac1..., mode c, seeds 20001..20040, 500 replicates per seed, 256 particles, row proposal counts 256/64/1024/64/64, 96 tail proposals, and the rule to use the one-sided 99% normal lower bound on the mean of all 20,000 linear replicate estimates whatever it was. No listed seed ran first and there was no interim look or fallback. All 20,000 estimates were positive. The linear mean was 1.49718785089645326e-29 = 2^-95.75365951; sample sd 4.01934149027624993e-30; the registered bound was 1.49057612917370439e-29 = 2^-95.76004469, rounded down to -95.7601. After seeing those data, a 40-seed cluster sensitivity treated each seed's 500-replicate linear mean as one observation. Its one-sided 99% Student lower bound was 1.49081383872899396e-29 = 2^-95.75981464, rounded down to -95.7599. The package takes the smaller linear bound, the preregistered replicate-level result, so q3_model remains 2^-95.7601. The estimator checks the counted rows 16..21 without E18=E17 and without row-19 proposal relations; its W23-in-F23, E22[29]=0, zero-difference tail is a sub-event. Its batch and lane draw is uniform on all 958,464 variants. The Python port now uses exact rejection for every bounded draw and one exact uniform variant index mapped by cumulative class sizes. The final organizer-request preregistration SHA-256 is 93f68ef3...2610: eight replicates, 32 particles, row proposals 64/16/256/16/16, 24 tail proposals, threshold -101.0 and zero failed checks. On 2,000 fresh identically configured C requests, 1,994 passed; the one-sided 99% exact pass-probability lower bound was 0.992730288977. The failed four-replicate sizing attempt and the cancelled round-2 calibration are retained but unused.
heuristics.limitations: The preregistered 99% figure uses a normal approximation over replicate estimates; it is not a distribution-free coverage theorem. The seed-level Student analysis was chosen after seeing the data, so it is a sensitivity check, not a preregistered replacement. Taking the smaller of its bound and the preregistered bound is conservative for this package. The C processes use deterministic xoshiro streams from distinct integer seeds. The estimator measures a lower-bound tail sub-event, so it may omit accepted collisions. The organizer experiment checks the port and rebuilt witnesses but supplies no trusted q3 probability inference. No full collision is expected at this scale.

heuristics.statement: Let R_f be the number of selected variants of first block f that are good and pass row 16, and A_t the event that trial t = (f, a0) succeeds. The declared premise is the 8-class bound of the accepted filing, E[R_f - 1 | success] <= 2^-7.5, scaled by the variant-count ratio 958,464/196,608 = 4.875 for this revision: <= 2^-5.2146. The Bonferroni factor of the per-first-block bound is therefore (1 - 2^-6.2146) E[X_f].
heuristics.scope: The per-first-block Bonferroni bound Pr[X_f >= 1] >= E[X_f] - E[X_f (X_f - 1)]/2 >= (1 - 2^-6.2146) E[X_f] (proof.md Section 10).
heuristics.extrapolation: Under H1 the law of (CV1, a0) given a success is the law of the successes of the Step-3 sampler (proof.md Section 13.5). Our measurement on successes of the accepted event: 12,028 successes of 8 independent runs of the replica's sampler (the 8 classes, a0 uniform on the 196,608 variants), each rebuilt into a verified pair and accepted by step3b, every selected variant of every passing class of its chaining value tested: 32 other row-16 passes against 21.95 under independence, 2^-8.55 per success, one-sided 99% upper bounds 2^-7.97 (Poisson) and 2^-7.79 (Student over the 8 runs), below the 8-class premise 2^-7.5. For this revision the ledger charges the *premise* scaled by the variant ratio: 2^-7.5 x 4.875 = 2^-5.2146, i.e. a Bonferroni factor 1 - 2^-6.2146 (H3M in the shipped program), which costs 0.0155 bit; the measured 2^-8.55 scaled is 2^-6.26, 1.05 bit below the premise. This is a bound scaled to the larger variant set, not a re-measurement: the conditioning experiment used the 8 classes.
heuristics.limitations: The successes are sampled by the replica's sampler, a sub-event of the accepted event (row-19 relation sets, W23 in F23, zero differences from row 22), not real collisions; successes within a run share ancestors (the Student bound uses the 8 independent runs). The other row-16 passes exceed independence by a factor 1.46 (z = +2.15); the premise counts row-16 passes only, which is conservative. The 48-class value is the 8-class premise scaled by the variant ratio (a bound), not a measurement on the 48-class set; the measured 8-class value scaled is far below it.

heuristics.statement: The total computation spent to obtain the characteristic P8 of 1a695f0b (its signed-difference SAT sweep, coupling checks and estimators; failed and repeated runs included) is at most A_C = 2^56 target compressions.
heuristics.scope: The preprocessing part of the ledger: A_C = 2^56 is 12.4 bits above P8's own published search bound of 2^43.61 units; it enters the claimed time and preprocessing (57.58496).
heuristics.extrapolation: P8's search is published with its run log (1a695f0b Section 3.2, quoted; participant-run): 38 solver runs of at most 10,800 s (230,183 s in all), P8 found in 4,714 s with a 662-s coupling check; its author bounds the search, S, the class data and all development by one 10-core machine for less than 2^21 core-seconds, which at our measured 3,797,484 SHA-256 compressions per second is 2^43.61 units, 12.4 bits under A_C = 2^56. Our own measurements of the same kind of search (proof.md Appendix C, from fb176310): a 39-step characteristic derived from scratch with the public tool of [LLW24] in 2^36.04 units; published figures up to 2^39.15 units, 16.85 bits under A_C. A_C = 2^56 leaves at least 12.4 bits over P8's own search for unrecorded failed and repeated runs; it replaces fb176310's inherited 2^78.
heuristics.limitations: An allowance, not our measurement: we did not rerun P8's search; its log and the 2^21 core-second bound are the author's. With A_C = 2^84 the claim would be 85.20307.

heuristics.statement: S (the dense part of P8's semi-free-start pair) and the 8 class descriptors with their product description are obtained at a total cost of at most A_S = 2^56 target compressions.
heuristics.scope: The preprocessing part of the ledger (A_S = 2^56, well below 0.001% of T); it is more than 20 bits above the 662-s coupling check.
heuristics.extrapolation: 1a695f0b obtained the pair in its 662-s coupling check and the class descriptors by 32 passes over a hash of c7 (quoted); our exhaustive pass over all 2^32 values of a0 (p8fam.c, 102 s, 69 MB peak) reproduces the 8 classes and their 24,576 members each, and selftest checks the product description. A_S = 2^56 is more than 20 bits above the 662-s coupling check and replaces fb176310's inherited 2^74.
heuristics.limitations: An allowance: the pair search was run by 1a695f0b, not by us; its sampled memory peak was 2^28.0936238847 bytes and the claim allows 2^28.1 bytes (H6).

heuristics.statement: All development of this package, including inherited searches and checks, the new source audit, 20,000-replicate direct q3 measurement, matched C check, executor port runs, and ledger reproduction, is at most DEV = 2^56 target compressions. H4c is a time charge; memory is H6.
heuristics.scope: The development item of the ledger (DEV = 2^56, well below 0.001% of T).
heuristics.extrapolation: Recorded development below 1.5 x 10^5 CPU-seconds (proof.md Section 13.4); at 10^10 word operations per CPU-second that is below 2^51 operations = 2^39.3 compressions, so 2^56 is more than 2^16 times the recorded work. Every development execution whose output the claim uses ran under a hard address-space cap of 2^27 or 2^28 bytes with its peak measured by memmeter (the shared-carrier runs of proof.md Section 7.5 by /usr/bin/time -v, at most 2^27.74 bytes), at most 2^27.77 bytes (proof.md Section 14 (c2), Appendix A.10).
heuristics.limitations: Accounting of participant-run work, not an organizer work log. The new C measurement took 203.81 wall seconds with at most four single-threaded processes and is negligible beside the inherited DEV allowance.

heuristics.statement: Under collision-frontier-v5, a straight-line word-RAM program that evaluates E16x = C16 + W0 + s0(W1) and its stage-3a test for 256 variants at once (bit L of every 256-bit word belongs to variant L) is charged its instruction list: every load, store and spill is counted, 64 registers, complements are free except in a mixed and/or (one more operation), no fused AND-NOT; one stage-2 program per batch, with the batch's constant bits of a0 folded into it, and one stage-1 program per (class, G1) whose stored planes the 32 stage-2 programs of its y values load (each store and each load is an instruction and is counted); no target compression is evaluated this way.
heuristics.scope: The plane-program term of the ledger (100,870.46 of the 118,253.49 data-dependent operations per first block).
heuristics.extrapolation: The 144 stage-1 and 3,744 stage-2 programs are generated and counted by experiments/a0hoist38.py (build_e16, group, Prog.schedule, run_prog): 2,428 to 3,355 instructions per stage-1 program (mean 2,894.88) and 270 to 303 per stage-2 program (mean 285.17, 0 spills in stage 2, at most 98 spill slots in stage 1); the organizer experiment a0-online-r38 executes 624 stage-2 programs of all four group sizes (20, 24, 28, 32 batches) with their stage-1 programs on all 256 lanes and compares them with the scalar definition (159,744 lanes in trials 6..13 plus 138,240 lanes in trials 0..5 in the local emulation, 0 mismatches), and all 3,744 stage-2 programs (958,464 lanes) are verified against the scalar definition with 0 mismatches.
heuristics.limitations: No organizer ruling is cited; the same reading was accepted for fb176310 and 2d1c4fc2. Program generation is charged 2^32 operations per program, not counted instruction by instruction. With a scalar evaluation (38 operations per variant) the claim would be 89.42650.

heuristics.statement: Peak memory is the maximum over counted phases and is claimed as 2^28.1 bytes. The inherited online program uses 47,752,640 bytes; inherited development peaks are at most 2^27.77 bytes; the largest reported phase is the P8 Step-1 solve, sampled by its author at 279,720 KiB = 286,433,280 bytes = 2^28.0936238847. The new C estimator used 17,396 KiB in the 20,000-replicate runner, and the Python port must remain inside the organizer's 128 MiB limit.
heuristics.scope: The memory metric and scalar score 84.26595 + (28.1 - 20) = 92.36595.
heuristics.extrapolation: The leading derivative section gives the exact byte conversion and new-run evidence. Inherited proof Section 14 inventories online code, tables, advice, solver instances and capped development. Appendix D.8 gives the 47,752,640-byte 48-class online program. The Step-1 measurement exceeds every other listed phase. The claimed 28.1 is an allowance above the sampled 28.0936238847 peak, not a claim that sampling found a hard maximum.
heuristics.limitations: The 279,720 KiB peak is the predecessor author's sampled resident-memory measurement at 0.2-second intervals, not ours and not a hard address-space cap. The 28.1 claim retains 0.006376 bit of allowance above that sampled value.

heuristics.statement: In the hoisting step, two Boolean DAG nodes of the batch programs of a (class, G1) group with equal 512-bit evaluation-and-structure signatures compute the same function (no false equivalence), so merging them leaves the generated program equal to the unhoisted one.
heuristics.scope: The node merging of the hoisted plane program (proof.md Section 9, hoisting): whether the generated program computes the reference row-16 filter. The counted operations are those of the generated program as written, exact whatever it computes; a false merge could only change which pairs pass the filter, hence the success probability, and every output is verified with the target.
heuristics.extrapolation: Our theory. Each gate mixes its 512-bit truth-table value with the symmetric product of its two input signatures, preventing carry-masking collisions across batches, and the generated programs agree bit for bit with the scalar reference on all 958,464 lanes of the 48 classes (0 disagreements) and on the organizer experiment a0-online-r38 (297,984 lanes across trials 0..13, 0 mismatches).
heuristics.limitations: Our theory, not a theorem: equal 512-bit evaluation signatures are taken to mean equal functions. Checked on 23,592,960 cloud lanes and the organizer's 196,608 lanes with 0 disagreements, not on all inputs.

restrictions: Target sha256-r38-prefix-v1 exactly: SHA-256 steps 0..37 on every padded block, the standard IV once, FIPS 180-4 padding, feed-forward, all eight digest words. Output: two distinct complete 128-byte messages M0||M1 and M0||M1' (common first block; FIPS padding appends the same third block) with equal digests; every output is a verified collision of the target (Lemma 6.1, proof.md Section 6.1).

Algorithm: the two-block attack of ePrint 2026/1120 with the characteristic P8 of dariolina's 1a695f0b (its cells, its semi-free-start pair, the Step-1 solution S; member x = M) and the A0-variant method of fb176310 and 2d1c4fc2, with the class set of Appendix D.4: 48 H-closed c7 classes (958,464 variants; 12 each of 24,576, 21,504, 18,432 and 15,360 members), each a union of 3 G1 groups of batches of 256 lanes. One W7 test decides a class and every variant of a passing class is a good pair; per (class, G1) one stage-1 program computes the planes shared by >= 2 batches of the group and 3,744 straight-line stage-2 batch programs fold the batch constants, evaluate E16x for 256 variants and test the 8 lowest bits shared by the 160 row-16 words; passing lanes resolved in scalar form; a row-16 pass checked through row 21 (row 19 on its signed differences only, E18 = E17 not imposed); rows 22..37 computed untested and both outputs compared (proof.md Section 6.1).

Cost: fixed caps. N_FB = 524,289,452,868,292,446,773,096 first blocks, each one target compression plus 35 counted operations; V_MAX = 62,000,001,702,237,770,704,753,973,184 data-dependent operations, tested at every block and after every class, with OVER = 301,467. A_C = A_S = DEV = 2^56; PRE = 16,698,832,871,424 operations; final verification is unchanged. The exact total numerator is 63,448,614,050,232,229,040,423,456,515 = T x 2728, so log2 T = 84.2659473785 and time_log2 = 84.26595.

Success probability at least 0.39 under H1, direct H2 q3_model = 2^-95.7601, H3 Bonferroni factor 1 - 2^-6.2146, and the unchanged Chebyshev cap. The direct q3 value is the preregistered one-sided 99% normal lower bound rounded down; the prior printed-cell-times-ratio composite is not used.

Memory: peak allowance 2^28.1 bytes, above the inherited author-sampled Step-1 peak 279,720 KiB = 286,433,280 bytes = 2^28.0936238847. Online memory remains 47,752,640 bytes and inherited development peaks remain below it. Nonuniform advice is unchanged at 18,624 bytes < 2^15. Scalar score = 92.36595.
